1	#ifndef SG_FUSED_SM90_TP_TRANSPORT_CUH_
2	#define SG_FUSED_SM90_TP_TRANSPORT_CUH_
3	// ============================================================================
4	// csrc/fused/sm_90/tp_transport.cuh — the TENSOR-PARALLEL TRANSPORT SEAM.
5	//
6	// IMPLEMENTS: /workspace/.parallelism_design.md §5.2 (device-initiated all-reduce
7	// inside the persistent megakernel, FIXED-ORDER so the cross-rank A/A/A gate
8	// §6.4 holds) + §5.3/§5.4 (the transport go/no-go is an IMPLEMENTATION choice;
9	// the TP math is transport-agnostic). Authored 1-GPU/CPU per design §7; task #25
10	// phase-2 authoring (Lane C).
11	//
12	// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
13	//  THE TRANSPORT SWAP POINT (read this first)
14	//
15	//  The TP all-reduce math (tp_layer.cuh) is written against ONE device-side
16	//  concept, `TpTransport`:
17	//
18	//      int     my_pe()  const            — this rank's index in the TP group
19	//      int     n_pes()  const            — TP group size
20	//      float*  local(int64_t off)        — THIS pe's buffer at symmetric offset
21	//      const float* peer(int64_t off,p)  — pe p's buffer at the SAME offset
22	//      (rendezvous)                      — the caller's GridBarrier + (real
23	//                                          multi-GPU only) the cross-GPU barrier
24	//                                          via Transport::rendezvous(bar)
25	//
26	//  TWO implementations live here:
27	//
28	//  * `LoopbackTransport` — the SINGLE-PROCESS, single-GPU loopback. The
29	//    "symmetric heap" is ONE device allocation of n_pes * stride floats; virtual
30	//    pe p's region is base + p*stride. All virtual PEs run in ONE grid (the CTAs
31	//    are partitioned into contiguous per-PE groups), so the cross-PE rendezvous
32	//    IS the existing GridBarrier over the whole grid. This is an HONEST
33	//    simulation: the TP math (shard GEMMs, partial publish, fixed-order
34	//    ascending-pe fp32 reduce) executes the IDENTICAL code path it executes on
35	//    NVSHMEM — the only thing swapped is (a) the symmetric-address translation
36	//    and (b) the rendezvous scope, which is precisely the transport abstraction.
37	//    It is NOT fake success: the loopback test (tests/hw/test_tp_loopback.py)
38	//    asserts bit-exact cross-virtual-rank identity + A/A/A + an exact-slice dW
39	//    check against the unsharded reference — failures fail loudly.
40	//
41	//  * `NvshmemTransport` — the REAL device-initiated NVSHMEM transport (design
42	//    §5.2). NVSHMEM IS NOT INSTALLED ON THIS BOX (verified 2026-06-12: no
43	//    headers/libs/pip/ldconfig hits), so this struct compiles ONLY under
44	//    -DSG_HAS_NVSHMEM=1 with the NVSHMEM toolkit on the include/link path. It is
45	//    NOT a stub that pretends to work: without the flag it does not exist, and
46	//    any attempt to instantiate the megakernel TP point with it is a loud
47	//    compile error pointing here. Wiring + validating it is the ONE genuinely
48	//    8×H100 task (design §7.5) — swap `LoopbackTransport` → `NvshmemTransport`
49	//    at the call sites and run the §5.4 go/no-go gate.
50	//
51	//  WHY offset-based symmetric addressing (not raw pointers): NVSHMEM's
52	//  symmetric heap guarantees the SAME offset is valid on every PE
53	//  (nvshmem_malloc returns symmetric addresses; nvshmem_ptr(sym, pe) translates
54	//  for NVLink load/store). The loopback reproduces exactly that property with
55	//  base + pe*stride. One addressing model ⇒ one math code path.
56	//
57	//  DETERMINISM (design §5.2, non-negotiable): the fixed-order all-reduce below
58	//  reads every PE's partial in ASCENDING pe order and accumulates fp32. The
59	//  summation order is STRUCTURAL (never timing-dependent), so the result is
60	//  bit-identical on every PE and across reruns — the cross-rank analogue of the
61	//  in-kernel ascending-CTA reduce that made the single-GPU path A/A/A.
62	//  A `nvshmem_float_sum_reduce` collective is deliberately NOT used (its
63	//  reduction order is unspecified) — on NVSHMEM the same ascending-pe loop runs
64	//  over nvshmem_ptr-translated peer pointers (NVLink direct load/store).
65	// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
66	//
67	// HEADER-ONLY, self-contained: CUDA runtime + the GridBarrier substrate only.
68	// No torch, no NCCL. Compiles for sm_90a with plain nvcc.
69	// ============================================================================
70	
71	#include <cstdint>
72	#include <cuda_runtime.h>
73	
74	#include "csrc/fused/megakernel_common.cuh"   // GridBarrier (the in-kernel rendezvous)
75	
76	#if defined(SG_HAS_NVSHMEM)
77	// Real NVSHMEM headers — present ONLY when the toolkit is installed and the
78	// build opts in. NOT installed on the authoring box (see header comment).
79	#include <nvshmem.h>
80	#include <nvshmemx.h>
81	#endif
82	
83	namespace sg { namespace fused { namespace sm90 { namespace tp {
84	
85	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
86	//  LoopbackTransport — single-process symmetric-heap simulation (the 1-GPU
87	//  honest test transport). See the swap-point doc above.
88	//
89	//  Host side: allocate ONE device buffer of `n_pes * stride_floats` floats and
90	//  pass (base, stride_floats, n_pes). Device side: each CTA derives its virtual
91	//  pe from its blockIdx (contiguous CTA groups per PE — `pe_of_cta`).
92	//  The rendezvous is the caller's whole-grid GridBarrier (all virtual PEs share
93	//  the grid), so `rendezvous()` simply forwards to bar.sync().
94	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
95	struct LoopbackTransport {
96	    float*  heap_base;       // [n_pes * stride_floats] device alloc
97	    int64_t stride_floats;   // per-PE symmetric region size
98	    int     n_pes_;          // TP degree being simulated
99	    int     my_pe_;          // this CTA-group's virtual rank
100	
101	    __device__ __forceinline__ int my_pe() const { return my_pe_; }
102	    __device__ __forceinline__ int n_pes() const { return n_pes_; }
103	
104	    // THIS pe's buffer at symmetric offset `off`.
105	    __device__ __forceinline__ float* local(int64_t off) const {
106	        return heap_base + (int64_t)my_pe_ * stride_floats + off;
107	    }
108	    // Peer pe's buffer at the SAME symmetric offset (ascending-pe reads in the
109	    // fixed-order reduce). On NVSHMEM this is nvshmem_ptr(sym, pe); here it is
110	    // the strided region — same contract, swapped translation.
111	    __device__ __forceinline__ const float* peer(int64_t off, int pe) const {
112	        return heap_base + (int64_t)pe * stride_floats + off;
113	    }
114	
115	    // Cross-PE rendezvous. Loopback: every virtual PE lives in THIS grid, so the
116	    // whole-grid GridBarrier IS the cross-PE barrier (publish partials → sync →
117	    // read peers → sync → reuse slots).
118	    __device__ __forceinline__ void rendezvous(const ::sg::fused::GridBarrier& bar) const {
119	        bar.sync();
120	    }
121	
122	    // Static CTA→PE partition helper: contiguous CTA groups (CTA c of nCTA, P
123	    // pes → pe = c / (nCTA/P); caller guarantees nCTA % P == 0, asserted in the
124	    // launchers). Contiguity keeps each virtual rank's tile traversal identical
125	    // to a real per-GPU grid (ascending tiles within the rank).
126	    __host__ __device__ __forceinline__ static int pe_of_cta(int cta, int nCTA, int P) {
127	        return cta / (nCTA / P);
128	    }
129	    __host__ __device__ __forceinline__ static int cta_within_pe(int cta, int nCTA, int P) {
130	        return cta % (nCTA / P);
131	    }
132	    __host__ __device__ __forceinline__ static int ctas_per_pe(int nCTA, int P) {
133	        return nCTA / P;
134	    }
135	};
136	
137	#if defined(SG_HAS_NVSHMEM)
138	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
139	//  NvshmemTransport — the REAL device-initiated transport (design §5.2).
140	//  COMPILED ONLY under -DSG_HAS_NVSHMEM=1 (toolkit on the path). The math code
141	//  path is IDENTICAL to the loopback's; only the address translation + the
142	//  rendezvous scope differ:
143	//    * `heap_base` is an nvshmem_malloc'd SYMMETRIC allocation (same offset
144	//      valid on every PE);
145	//    * `peer()` translates via nvshmem_ptr (NVLink direct load/store — the
146	//      single-node 8×H100 case; a multi-node fabric would use nvshmem_get,
147	//      which is the documented extension point, NOT silently emulated);
148	//    * `rendezvous()` = in-GPU GridBarrier + ONE CTA running the cross-GPU
149	//      nvshmemx_barrier_all_block + GridBarrier again (so every CTA of every
150	//      GPU is fenced both sides — the §5.2 "two barrier systems must not
151	//      deadlock" discipline: the NVSHMEM barrier is entered by exactly one CTA
152	//      per GPU, never concurrently with the GridBarrier spin).
153	//  GO/NO-GO (§5.4): parity vs host-NCCL TP, A/A/A, MFU, ZeRO-3/DP composition —
154	//  all 8×H100-window activities (design §7.5).
155	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
156	struct NvshmemTransport {
157	    float*  heap_base;       // nvshmem_malloc'd symmetric base (LOCAL pointer)
158	    int     n_pes_;          // TP group size  (nvshmem_n_pes() on the TP team)
159	    int     my_pe_;          // this GPU's pe  (nvshmem_my_pe())
160	
161	    __device__ __forceinline__ int my_pe() const { return my_pe_; }
162	    __device__ __forceinline__ int n_pes() const { return n_pes_; }
163	
164	    __device__ __forceinline__ float* local(int64_t off) const {
165	        return heap_base + off;
166	    }
167	    __device__ __forceinline__ const float* peer(int64_t off, int pe) const {
168	        // NVLink path: direct load/store through the peer mapping. nvshmem_ptr
169	        // returns nullptr for non-P2P-reachable peers — single-node 8×H100 is
170	        // always reachable; the multi-node fall-back (nvshmem_get staging) is
171	        // future work and must NOT be silently approximated here.
172	        return static_cast<const float*>(nvshmem_ptr(heap_base, pe)) + off;
173	    }
174	
175	    __device__ __forceinline__ void rendezvous(const ::sg::fused::GridBarrier& bar) const {
176	        bar.sync();                       // all CTAs of THIS GPU arrived
177	        if (blockIdx.x == 0) {            // one CTA crosses the GPU boundary
178	            nvshmemx_barrier_all_block();
179	        }
180	        bar.sync();                       // release every CTA after the cross-GPU join
181	    }
182	};
183	#endif  // SG_HAS_NVSHMEM
184	
185	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
186	//  tp_allreduce_sum_fixed_order — THE all-reduce both transports share.
187	//
188	//  PRE: every PE has PUBLISHED its fp32 partial at symmetric offset `slot_off`
189	//  (length n) and the caller has crossed `tr.rendezvous(bar)` once (so all
190	//  publishes are visible). POST: `dst[i] = Σ_pe partial_pe[i]`, summed in
191	//  ASCENDING pe order in fp32 — bit-identical on every PE and across reruns
192	//  (design §5.2/§2.7: structural order, the A/A/A non-negotiable). The caller
193	//  crosses `tr.rendezvous(bar)` again before REUSING the slot.
194	//
195	//  `tid`/`nthreads` define this PE's cooperative element loop. In the loopback
196	//  every virtual PE redundantly computes its own copy (each PE strides its own
197	//  CTA group's threads) — exactly what real per-GPU ranks do.
198	//
199	//  This is deliberately NOT nvshmem_float_sum_reduce: that collective's
200	//  reduction order is unspecified ⇒ ULP drift run-to-run ⇒ A/A/A failure
201	//  (design §5.2). The hand-rolled ascending-pe loop IS the deliverable.
202	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
203	template <class Transport>
204	__device__ __forceinline__ void tp_allreduce_sum_fixed_order(
205	        const Transport& tr, int64_t slot_off, float* __restrict__ dst,
206	        int64_t n, int tid, int nthreads) {
207	    const int P = tr.n_pes();
208	    for (int64_t i = tid; i < n; i += nthreads) {
209	        float acc = 0.0f;
210	        #pragma unroll 1
211	        for (int pe = 0; pe < P; ++pe) {        // ASCENDING pe — fixed order
212	            acc += tr.peer(slot_off, pe)[i];
213	        }
214	        dst[i] = acc;
215	    }
216	}
217	
218	// Variant writing the reduced value back INTO this PE's symmetric slot (in-place
219	// consumers); same fixed order. Safe because every PE reads ALL peers before any
220	// PE can pass the post-reduce rendezvous the caller crosses before reuse — the
221	// read-before-overwrite hazard is what that second rendezvous exists for, so
222	// this variant must write to a DIFFERENT slot than it reads. Kept explicit:
223	template <class Transport>
224	__device__ __forceinline__ void tp_allreduce_sum_fixed_order_to_slot(
225	        const Transport& tr, int64_t src_slot_off, int64_t dst_slot_off,
226	        int64_t n, int tid, int nthreads) {
227	    float* dst = tr.local(dst_slot_off);
228	    tp_allreduce_sum_fixed_order(tr, src_slot_off, dst, n, tid, nthreads);
229	}
230	
231	}}}}  // namespace sg::fused::sm90::tp
232	
233	#endif  // SG_FUSED_SM90_TP_TRANSPORT_CUH_

1	"""grokking_optimizers.distributed — Stage 7 distributed-training layer (§8).
2	
3	This is a **Python-level orchestration layer** that sits on top of the existing
4	optimizers and the Stage-6 fused megakernel. It introduces **no kernel changes**
5	and does **not** touch any optimizer `.step()` math; it only wires the per-GPU
6	local compute into a multi-GPU / multinode rank mesh.
7	
8	Coverage of the §8 spec:
9	
10	* §8.1 — classic **3D parallelism**: data (DP) × tensor (TP) × pipeline (PP).
11	  There is deliberately **no sequence / 4th parallel dim** — the race models are
12	  short-sequence (arithmetic grokking, small ViT/Mamba), so a sequence split
13	  buys nothing and only adds all-to-all traffic. The mesh is the standard
14	  DP×TP×PP rank decomposition.
15	* §8.3 — **ZeRO-3** full optimizer-state sharding across the DP group (SG2's
16	  ~5–6× optimizer-state footprint, from the CSA/HCA + PEER meta-net, needs it).
17	* §8.4 — orchestration via **DeepSpeed (ZeRO-3) or Megatron-LM**, NCCL on
18	  NVIDIA / RCCL on AMD. The fused-kernel adapter that lets the Stage-6
19	  single-launch megakernel satisfy the framework's separate fwd/bwd/step
20	  interface lives in :mod:`grokking_optimizers.megakernel_engine` (the trickiest
21	  integration — see that module's docstring).
22	* §8.5 — the megakernel components are reused as the per-GPU *local* compute;
23	  this module's comms layer wraps them.
24	* §8.6 — multinode at maximal efficiency (InfiniBand / NVLink-class fabric).
25	  AMD multinode trails NVIDIA under ZeRO-3 cross-node all-gathers (§2.13); the
26	  config records the backend so the harness can attribute the gap.
27	
28	CRITICAL — **import safety**. Importing this module must succeed with no
29	distributed job launched, no GPU, and no DeepSpeed installed (the common case:
30	the self-test and `import grokking_optimizers`). Every `torch.distributed` call
31	is therefore guarded and lazy: nothing touches a process group at import time,
32	and a non-launched job degrades cleanly to a single-process world (world_size=1,
33	rank=0, all parallel dims = 1).
34	"""
35	
36	from __future__ import annotations
37	
38	import dataclasses
39	import os
40	from typing import Dict, Iterable, Optional, Tuple
41	
42	# torch is a hard dependency of the package (the optimizers need it), but we
43	# still touch torch.distributed only behind guards, since the *backend* (NCCL/
44	# RCCL/gloo) and a launched job are optional.
45	import torch
46	
47	
48	# ───────────────────────────── ParallelConfig ────────────────────────────────
49	
50	
51	@dataclasses.dataclass
52	class ParallelConfig:
53	    """Declarative description of the 3D-parallel + ZeRO mesh (§8.1, §8.3, §8.4).
54	
55	    The product ``data_parallel * tensor_parallel * pipeline_parallel`` must
56	    equal the launched ``world_size`` (validated lazily in
57	    :meth:`DistributedContext.from_config`, never at import).
58	
59	    Attributes
60	    ----------
61	    data_parallel, tensor_parallel, pipeline_parallel:
62	        Sizes of the three parallel dims. ``1`` disables that dim. There is no
63	        sequence-parallel dim by design (short-sequence models, §8.1).
64	    expert_parallel:
65	        Size of the expert-parallel (EP) dim — the MoE experts are sharded
66	        across this many ranks (the PEER/MoE optimizers, e.g.
67	        ``MoEAwareSuperGrok2``, route tokens to expert shards). ``1`` (the
68	        default) disables EP, so the common dense case is unaffected. EP shares
69	        ranks with the DP group (experts are replicated/sharded over the same
70	        data-parallel ranks), so it does NOT enlarge ``world_size``; instead it
71	        sub-divides the DP dim (``data_parallel`` must be a multiple of
72	        ``expert_parallel``). The EP group is the set of DP peers that together
73	        hold one full expert set.
74	    zero_stage:
75	        ZeRO optimizer-state sharding stage, 0/1/2/3. Stage 3 shards optimizer
76	        state **and** gradients **and** parameters across the DP group (§8.3).
77	        Sharding is always over the DP group (TP/PP shard the model itself).
78	    backend:
79	        Collective backend. ``"nccl"`` on NVIDIA, ``"rccl"`` on AMD (ROCm ships
80	        RCCL behind the same ``"nccl"`` ProcessGroup name — see
81	        :meth:`resolved_backend`), ``"gloo"`` for CPU-only smoke tests.
82	    use_megakernel:
83	        When True, the per-GPU local compute is the Stage-6 fused megakernel and
84	        the framework is driven through the
85	        :mod:`grokking_optimizers.megakernel_engine` adapter (§8.4/§8.5).
86	    reduce_bucket_size:
87	        Target size, in **elements**, of the flat gradient buckets the native
88	        DDP all-reduce coalesces small per-param gradients into (§8.4). Larger
89	        buckets amortize per-collective launch latency at the cost of delaying
90	        the first reduce; ~25M elements (≈50 MB bf16 / 100 MB fp32) is a sane
91	        default for the race's small models. Honored by
92	        :meth:`DistributedContext.all_reduce_dp_grads` and the async-overlap
93	        grad hooks.
94	    """
95	
96	    data_parallel: int = 1
97	    tensor_parallel: int = 1
98	    pipeline_parallel: int = 1
99	    expert_parallel: int = 1
100	    zero_stage: int = 0
101	    backend: str = "nccl"
102	    use_megakernel: bool = True
103	    reduce_bucket_size: int = 25_000_000
104	
105	    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
106	        for name in ("data_parallel", "tensor_parallel", "pipeline_parallel",
107	                     "expert_parallel"):
108	            v = getattr(self, name)
109	            if not isinstance(v, int) or v < 1:
110	                raise ValueError(f"{name} must be a positive int, got {v!r}")
111	        if self.zero_stage not in (0, 1, 2, 3):
112	            raise ValueError(f"zero_stage must be 0/1/2/3, got {self.zero_stage}")
113	        if not isinstance(self.reduce_bucket_size, int) or self.reduce_bucket_size < 1:
114	            raise ValueError(
115	                f"reduce_bucket_size must be a positive int, "
116	                f"got {self.reduce_bucket_size!r}")
117	        # EP sub-divides the DP dim (experts are sharded over DP peers), so it
118	        # must evenly divide it and never exceeds it.
119	        if self.data_parallel % self.expert_parallel != 0:
120	            raise ValueError(
121	                f"expert_parallel ({self.expert_parallel}) must evenly divide "
122	                f"data_parallel ({self.data_parallel}) — EP shards experts "
123	                f"across a subset of the DP ranks.")
124	
125	    @property
126	    def ep(self) -> int:
127	        """Alias for ``expert_parallel`` (the short spelling used in configs)."""
128	        return self.expert_parallel
129	
130	    @property
131	    def model_parallel_size(self) -> int:
132	        """TP×PP — the number of ranks one full model copy is spread across."""
133	        return self.tensor_parallel * self.pipeline_parallel
134	
135	    @property
136	    def world_size(self) -> int:
137	        """Total ranks the config describes (DP×TP×PP)."""
138	        return self.data_parallel * self.tensor_parallel * self.pipeline_parallel
139	
140	    def resolved_backend(self) -> str:
141	        """Map the logical backend to the torch ProcessGroup backend string.
142	
143	        ROCm's RCCL registers under the *same* ``"nccl"`` ProcessGroup backend
144	        name (torch dispatches NCCL↔RCCL by the build, not the string), so
145	        ``"rccl"`` resolves to ``"nccl"`` for :func:`torch.distributed.init_process_group`.
146	        """
147	        return "nccl" if self.backend in ("nccl", "rccl") else self.backend
148	
149	    def validate_against_world(self, world_size: int) -> None:
150	        """Raise if DP×TP×PP does not match the launched ``world_size``."""
151	        if self.world_size != world_size:
152	            raise ValueError(
153	                f"ParallelConfig DP×TP×PP = {self.data_parallel}×"
154	                f"{self.tensor_parallel}×{self.pipeline_parallel} = "
155	                f"{self.world_size} does not match launched world_size={world_size}"
156	            )
157	
158	
159	# ──────────────────────── distributed availability probes ─────────────────────
160	
161	
162	def _dist():
163	    """Return ``torch.distributed`` if importable, else ``None`` (no crash)."""
164	    try:
165	        import torch.distributed as dist  # noqa: PLC0415 — lazy by design
166	    except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - torch always ships dist, defensive
167	        return None
168	    return dist
169	
170	
171	def is_dist_available_and_initialized() -> bool:
172	    """True only when a real process group has been launched & initialized.
173	
174	    This is the single guard every collective in this module funnels through, so
175	    the not-launched case (self-test, plain import) short-circuits to a no-op.
176	    """
177	    dist = _dist()
178	    return bool(dist) and dist.is_available() and dist.is_initialized()
179	
180	
181	def _env_int(name: str, default: int) -> int:
182	    try:
183	        return int(os.environ.get(name, default))
184	    except (TypeError, ValueError):
185	        return default
186	
187	
188	def _bucketize(tensors, bucket_elems: int):
189	    """Group ``tensors`` into contiguous buckets of ~``bucket_elems`` elements.
190	
191	    A single tensor larger than the target still forms its own (oversized)
192	    bucket so nothing is dropped. Order is preserved so the flat-buffer
193	    scatter-back in :meth:`DistributedContext.all_reduce_dp_grads` stays
194	    aligned. Pure-Python list math (no collectives) — unit-testable offline.
195	    """
196	    bucket: list = []
197	    cur = 0
198	    for t in tensors:
199	        n = t.numel()
200	        if bucket and cur + n > bucket_elems:
201	            yield bucket
202	            bucket, cur = [], 0
203	        bucket.append(t)
204	        cur += n
205	    if bucket:
206	        yield bucket
207	
208	
209	# ───────────────────────────── DistributedContext ────────────────────────────
210	
211	
212	@dataclasses.dataclass
213	class _RankMesh:
214	    """The (dp, tp, pp) coordinates of this rank plus the per-dim peer ranks.
215	
216	    Rank-linearization order is the Megatron-LM convention: the fastest-varying
217	    dim is TP, then PP, then DP (``rank = ((dp * pp_size + pp) * tp_size + tp)``).
218	    Keeping TP contiguous puts the high-traffic tensor-parallel all-reduces on
219	    the tightest fabric (intra-node NVLink/Infinity-Fabric), which is what §8.6
220	    wants for maximal efficiency.
221	    """
222	
223	    global_rank: int
224	    world_size: int
225	    dp: int
226	    tp: int
227	    pp: int
228	    ep: int
229	    dp_ranks: Tuple[int, ...]
230	    tp_ranks: Tuple[int, ...]
231	    pp_ranks: Tuple[int, ...]
232	    ep_ranks: Tuple[int, ...]
233	
234	
235	def _coords_from_rank(rank: int, dp: int, tp: int, pp: int) -> Tuple[int, int, int]:
236	    """Decompose a global rank into (dp, tp, pp) coords (TP fastest, then PP)."""
237	    tp_i = rank % tp
238	    pp_i = (rank // tp) % pp
239	    dp_i = rank // (tp * pp)
240	    return dp_i, tp_i, pp_i
241	
242	
243	def _rank_from_coords(dp_i: int, tp_i: int, pp_i: int, dp: int, tp: int, pp: int) -> int:
244	    return (dp_i * pp + pp_i) * tp + tp_i
245	
246	
247	def _build_mesh(rank: int, cfg: ParallelConfig) -> _RankMesh:
248	    """Pure-Python rank-mesh math (no collectives) — testable without a launch.
249	
250	    Computes this rank's (dp,tp,pp) coords and the peer-rank lists for each of
251	    the three subgroups it belongs to. The actual ``new_group`` calls happen in
252	    :meth:`DistributedContext._init_groups`; this keeps the index arithmetic
253	    unit-testable on a single process.
254	    """
255	    dp, tp, pp = cfg.data_parallel, cfg.tensor_parallel, cfg.pipeline_parallel
256	    ep = cfg.expert_parallel
257	    dp_i, tp_i, pp_i = _coords_from_rank(rank, dp, tp, pp)
258	
259	    # DP peers: vary dp_i, hold (tp_i, pp_i) — this is the ZeRO-3 shard group.
260	    dp_ranks = tuple(
261	        _rank_from_coords(d, tp_i, pp_i, dp, tp, pp) for d in range(dp)
262	    )
263	    # TP peers: vary tp_i, hold (dp_i, pp_i) — the per-layer all-reduce group.
264	    tp_ranks = tuple(
265	        _rank_from_coords(dp_i, t, pp_i, dp, tp, pp) for t in range(tp)
266	    )
267	    # PP peers: vary pp_i, hold (dp_i, tp_i) — the pipeline-stage send/recv group.
268	    pp_ranks = tuple(
269	        _rank_from_coords(dp_i, tp_i, p, dp, tp, pp) for p in range(pp)
270	    )
271	    # EP peers: the ``ep`` consecutive DP ranks that together hold one full
272	    # (sharded) expert set. DP is partitioned into dp/ep expert-replica blocks;
273	    # this rank's EP group is the block its dp_i falls in. EP coordinate is the
274	    # offset within that block. EP size 1 ⇒ a singleton group (no-op).
275	    ep_block_start = (dp_i // ep) * ep
276	    ep_dp_coords = range(ep_block_start, ep_block_start + ep)
277	    ep_ranks = tuple(
278	        _rank_from_coords(d, tp_i, pp_i, dp, tp, pp) for d in ep_dp_coords
279	    )
280	    ep_i = dp_i % ep
281	    return _RankMesh(
282	        global_rank=rank,
283	        world_size=cfg.world_size,
284	        dp=dp_i,
285	        tp=tp_i,
286	        pp=pp_i,
287	        ep=ep_i,
288	        dp_ranks=dp_ranks,
289	        tp_ranks=tp_ranks,
290	        pp_ranks=pp_ranks,
291	        ep_ranks=ep_ranks,
292	    )

295	class DistributedContext:
296	    """Lazily-initialized holder of the DP/TP/PP process groups (§8.1).
297	
298	    Construction never touches ``torch.distributed``. Call :meth:`initialize`
299	    (or use :meth:`from_config`, which initializes) inside a launched job to
300	    build the subgroups. With no launched job everything degrades to a
301	    single-process world: ``world_size == 1``, ``rank == 0``, every parallel dim
302	    collapses to size 1, and every collective helper becomes a no-op. That is
303	    exactly the self-test / plain-import path, and it must not crash.
304	    """
305	
306	    def __init__(self, config: Optional[ParallelConfig] = None) -> None:
307	        self.config = config or ParallelConfig(use_megakernel=False)
308	        self._initialized = False
309	        self._mesh: Optional[_RankMesh] = None
310	        # Per-dim process-group handles (opaque; None ⇒ WORLD / single-process).
311	        self._dp_group = None
312	        self._tp_group = None
313	        self._pp_group = None
314	        self._ep_group = None
315	        # Async DDP grad-hook bookkeeping (populated by register_dp_grad_hooks).
316	        self._dp_grad_hook_handles: list = []
317	        self._pending_dp_works: list = []
318	
319	    # ── construction / teardown ──────────────────────────────────────────────
320	
321	    @classmethod
322	    def from_config(cls, config: ParallelConfig) -> "DistributedContext":
323	        """Build a context and initialize its groups if a job is launched.
324	
325	        Safe to call with no launch: returns a single-process context.
326	        """
327	        ctx = cls(config)
328	        ctx.initialize()
329	        return ctx
330	
331	    def initialize(self, init_method: Optional[str] = None) -> "DistributedContext":
332	        """Initialize process groups *if and only if* a job is launched.
333	
334	        Idempotent. With no launch (or torch.distributed unavailable) this marks
335	        the context single-process and returns immediately — no collective is
336	        ever issued, so import/self-test paths are safe.
337	        """
338	        if self._initialized:
339	            return self
340	        dist = _dist()
341	
342	        # Single-process / not-launched path: build a degenerate 1-rank mesh.
343	        if dist is None or not dist.is_available():
344	            self._mesh = _build_mesh(0, ParallelConfig())
345	            self._initialized = True
346	            return self
347	
348	        # If the launcher set the env vars but the user has not yet called
349	        # init_process_group, initialize it lazily here (idempotent guard).
350	        if not dist.is_initialized():
351	            world_size = _env_int("WORLD_SIZE", 1)
352	            if world_size <= 1:
353	                # No real job — single process. Do NOT init a group.
354	                self._mesh = _build_mesh(0, ParallelConfig())
355	                self._initialized = True
356	                return self
357	            rank = _env_int("RANK", 0)
358	            backend = self.config.resolved_backend()
359	            try:
360	                dist.init_process_group(
361	                    backend=backend, init_method=init_method,
362	                    world_size=world_size, rank=rank,
363	                )
364	            except Exception:
365	                # A misconfigured launch should degrade, not hard-crash an
366	                # import-time path. Fall back to single-process.
367	                self._mesh = _build_mesh(0, ParallelConfig())
368	                self._initialized = True
369	                return self
370	
371	        rank = dist.get_rank()
372	        world_size = dist.get_world_size()
373	        self.config.validate_against_world(world_size)
374	        self._mesh = _build_mesh(rank, self.config)
375	        self._init_groups()
376	        self._initialized = True
377	        return self
378	
379	    def _init_groups(self) -> None:
380	        """Create the DP/TP/PP subgroups via ``new_group`` (launched-job only).
381	
382	        ``new_group`` is a **collective** that every rank must enter for every
383	        group, so we iterate the full set of subgroups deterministically and
384	        each rank keeps the handle for the group it belongs to. This is the
385	        standard Megatron-LM group-construction pattern.
386	        """
387	        dist = _dist()
388	        assert dist is not None and self._mesh is not None
389	        cfg = self.config
390	        dp, tp, pp = cfg.data_parallel, cfg.tensor_parallel, cfg.pipeline_parallel
391	        ep = cfg.expert_parallel
392	        mesh = self._mesh
393	
394	        # Build every DP group (one per (tp_i, pp_i) slice).
395	        for tp_i in range(tp):
396	            for pp_i in range(pp):
397	                ranks = [
398	                    _rank_from_coords(d, tp_i, pp_i, dp, tp, pp) for d in range(dp)
399	                ]
400	                g = dist.new_group(ranks)
401	                if mesh.global_rank in ranks:
402	                    self._dp_group = g
403	        # Build every EP group (one per (tp_i, pp_i, dp-block) slice): the ``ep``
404	        # consecutive DP ranks that hold one full expert set. Only meaningful
405	        # when ep > 1; with ep == 1 each group is a singleton (still entered by
406	        # every rank — new_group is collective). Skipped entirely for ep == 1 to
407	        # avoid issuing dp*tp*pp singleton-group collectives.
408	        if ep > 1:
409	            for tp_i in range(tp):
410	                for pp_i in range(pp):
411	                    for block_start in range(0, dp, ep):
412	                        ranks = [
413	                            _rank_from_coords(d, tp_i, pp_i, dp, tp, pp)
414	                            for d in range(block_start, block_start + ep)
415	                        ]
416	                        g = dist.new_group(ranks)
417	                        if mesh.global_rank in ranks:
418	                            self._ep_group = g
419	        # Build every TP group (one per (dp_i, pp_i) slice).
420	        for dp_i in range(dp):
421	            for pp_i in range(pp):
422	                ranks = [
423	                    _rank_from_coords(dp_i, t, pp_i, dp, tp, pp) for t in range(tp)
424	                ]
425	                g = dist.new_group(ranks)
426	                if mesh.global_rank in ranks:
427	                    self._tp_group = g
428	        # Build every PP group (one per (dp_i, tp_i) slice).
429	        for dp_i in range(dp):
430	            for tp_i in range(tp):
431	                ranks = [
432	                    _rank_from_coords(dp_i, tp_i, p, dp, tp, pp) for p in range(pp)
433	                ]
434	                g = dist.new_group(ranks)
435	                if mesh.global_rank in ranks:
436	                    self._pp_group = g

536	    def all_reduce_tp(self, tensor: "torch.Tensor") -> "torch.Tensor":
537	        """Sum-reduce a tensor across the tensor-parallel group (in place).
538	
539	        The per-layer all-reduce of a column/row-parallel Linear (§8.1 TP).
540	        No-op when TP size is 1 or no job is launched.
541	        """
542	        if self.tp_world_size > 1 and is_dist_available_and_initialized():
543	            _dist().all_reduce(tensor, group=self._tp_group)
544	        return tensor

546	    def all_reduce_ep(self, tensor: "torch.Tensor") -> "torch.Tensor":
547	        """Sum-reduce a tensor across the expert-parallel group (in place).
548	
549	        Used to combine partial expert outputs / expert-gradient stats across
550	        the EP shards that hold one full expert set. No-op when EP size is 1 or
551	        no job is launched.
552	        """
553	        if self.ep_world_size > 1 and is_dist_available_and_initialized():
554	            _dist().all_reduce(tensor, group=self._ep_group)

557	    def all_reduce_dp_grads(self, params: Iterable["torch.Tensor"]) -> None:
558	        """Average gradients across the DP group (the DDP gradient all-reduce).
559	
560	        Used for ZeRO-0/1/2, where gradients are replicated then averaged. Under
561	        ZeRO-3 the gradient is reduce-scattered instead (see
562	        :class:`ZeRO3Sharder`). No-op single-process.
563	
564	        Gradients are coalesced into flat buckets of ~``reduce_bucket_size``
565	        elements so a model with many small parameters issues a handful of large
566	        all-reduces instead of one per parameter — the per-collective launch
567	        latency is the dominant cost on the race's small models. Numerically
568	        identical to the prior per-param all-reduce (sum then divide by the DP
569	        world size); only the collective granularity changes.
570	        """
571	        if self.dp_world_size <= 1 or not is_dist_available_and_initialized():
572	            return
573	        dist = _dist()
574	        ws = self.dp_world_size
575	        grads = [p.grad for p in params if getattr(p, "grad", None) is not None]
576	        bucket_size = self.config.reduce_bucket_size
577	        for bucket in _bucketize(grads, bucket_size):
578	            if len(bucket) == 1:
579	                g = bucket[0]
580	                dist.all_reduce(g, group=self._dp_group)
581	                g.div_(ws)
582	                continue
583	            flat = torch.cat([g.reshape(-1) for g in bucket])
584	            dist.all_reduce(flat, group=self._dp_group)
585	            flat.div_(ws)
586	            # Scatter the reduced flat buffer back into each grad in place.
587	            offset = 0
588	            for g in bucket:
589	                n = g.numel()
590	                g.copy_(flat[offset:offset + n].view_as(g))
591	                offset += n
592	
593	    # ── async comm/compute overlap (DDP grad hooks) ──────────────────────────
594	
595	    def register_dp_grad_hooks(
596	        self, params: Iterable["torch.Tensor"]
597	    ) -> int:
598	        """Register backward hooks that issue **async** DP all-reduces.
599	
600	        Each parameter's ``register_post_accumulate_grad_hook`` fires the moment
601	        that grad finishes accumulating in backward, so the reduce overlaps with
602	        the remaining backward compute (comm/compute overlap, §8.4). The handles
603	        are returned via the count and tracked on the context;
604	        :meth:`wait_dp_grads` must be called before the optimizer step to drain
605	        the in-flight collectives and apply the ``1/world`` averaging.
606	
607	        No-op (returns 0) single-process or when the grad-hook API is missing.
608	        Returns the number of hooks registered.
609	        """
610	        if self.dp_world_size <= 1 or not is_dist_available_and_initialized():
611	            return 0
612	        self._pending_dp_works = getattr(self, "_pending_dp_works", [])
613	        self._dp_grad_hook_handles = getattr(self, "_dp_grad_hook_handles", [])
614	        ws = self.dp_world_size
615	        group = self._dp_group
616	        dist = _dist()
617	        count = 0
618	        for p in params:
619	            if not getattr(p, "requires_grad", False):
620	                continue
621	            if not hasattr(p, "register_post_accumulate_grad_hook"):
622	                # PyTorch < 2.1 — caller should use all_reduce_dp_grads instead.
623	                return count
624	
625	            def _hook(param, _ws=ws, _grp=group, _d=dist):
626	                if param.grad is None:
627	                    return
628	                work = _d.all_reduce(
629	                    param.grad, group=_grp, async_op=True)
630	                # Defer the /ws division until wait() so it lands after the
631	                # async reduce completes.
632	                self._pending_dp_works.append((work, param.grad, _ws))
633	
634	            self._dp_grad_hook_handles.append(
635	                p.register_post_accumulate_grad_hook(_hook))
636	            count += 1
637	        return count
638	
639	    def wait_dp_grads(self) -> None:
640	        """Wait on all in-flight async DP all-reduces and finish the averaging.
641	
642	        Call once after ``loss.backward()`` and before ``optimizer.step()``.
643	        Safe to call when no hooks were registered (no-op).
644	        """
645	        pending = getattr(self, "_pending_dp_works", None)
646	        if not pending:
647	            return
648	        for work, grad, ws in pending:
649	            if work is not None:
650	                work.wait()
651	            grad.div_(ws)
652	        pending.clear()
653	
654	    def remove_dp_grad_hooks(self) -> None:
655	        """Remove any registered DP grad hooks (best-effort)."""
656	        for h in getattr(self, "_dp_grad_hook_handles", []):
657	            try:
658	                h.remove()
659	            except Exception:
660	                pass
661	        self._dp_grad_hook_handles = []
662	        self._pending_dp_works = []

698	@dataclasses.dataclass
699	class _ParamShard:
700	    """Bookkeeping for one parameter's flat slice owned by this DP rank.
701	
702	    Under ZeRO-3 each DP rank owns a contiguous ``[start:end)`` slice of every
703	    parameter's flattened buffer (and, symmetrically, the same slice of every
704	    optimizer-state tensor for that param). ``numel`` is the full param size.
705	    """
706	
707	    name: str
708	    numel: int
709	    start: int
710	    end: int  # exclusive
711	
712	    @property
713	    def shard_numel(self) -> int:
714	        return self.end - self.start
715	
716	
717	def _even_partition(numel: int, world: int, rank: int) -> Tuple[int, int]:
718	    """Contiguous, padded-even partition of ``numel`` across ``world`` ranks.
719	
720	    Matches the DeepSpeed ZeRO-3 flat-partition convention: each rank owns
721	    ``ceil(numel/world)`` elements (the last rank's slice is clamped), so the
722	    union covers ``[0, numel)`` exactly with no overlap.
723	    """
724	    if world <= 1:
725	        return 0, numel
726	    per = (numel + world - 1) // world
727	    start = min(rank * per, numel)
728	    end = min(start + per, numel)
729	    return start, end

732	class ZeRO3Sharder:
733	    """§8.3 ZeRO-3 full optimizer-state sharding across the DP group.
734	
735	    Two backends, auto-selected:
736	
737	    * **DeepSpeed** — when importable, ZeRO-3 is best handled by DeepSpeed's
738	      `deepspeed.initialize(...)` engine (partitioned params + reduce-scatter
739	      gradients + all-gather-on-use, plus offload). We don't reimplement it; we
740	      hand back the framework-managed shape and the megakernel adapter (§8.4)
741	      plugs in as the `client_optimizer`. :meth:`build_ds_config` emits the
742	      matching ZeRO-3 config dict.
743	
744	    * **Native shim** — when DeepSpeed is absent, this class provides the same
745	      *pattern* with raw ``torch.distributed`` collectives:
746	
747	        - :meth:`partition_optimizer_state` assigns each DP rank a contiguous
748	          ``1/N`` slice of every param's optimizer state (m/v/etc.), so the
749	          aggregate state memory is ``1/N`` per rank — the win SG2's ~5–6×
750	          state footprint needs.
751	        - :meth:`reduce_scatter_grads` replaces the DP all-reduce: each rank
752	          ends up with the *reduced* gradient for **only its owned slice**
753	          (reduce-scatter), which is what the local optimizer step consumes.
754	        - :meth:`all_gather_params` reconstitutes the full parameter from the
755	          per-rank slices after the step (all-gather-on-step), so forward/
756	          backward see complete weights.
757	
758	    Both backends are import-safe and degrade to a no-op single-process shim
759	    (every collective short-circuits when DP size is 1 / no job launched).
760	
761	    DOCUMENTED PARTIAL STOP (cross-param flat-bucket ZeRO-3): the native shim
762	    now uses the fused per-parameter ``reduce_scatter_tensor`` /
763	    ``all_gather_into_tensor`` primitives (half the traffic of the old
764	    all-reduce-then-slice, and one collective call instead of a Python list
765	    gather). It still issues **one collective per parameter**. A further win
766	    would coalesce many small params into a single flat ~``reduce_bucket_size``
767	    bucket per reduce-scatter/all-gather (as DeepSpeed's ``contiguous_gradients``
768	    does). That is NOT implemented here: a correct cross-param bucketed
769	    reduce-scatter must reproduce DeepSpeed's exact per-rank ownership of the
770	    *concatenated* buffer (padding + alignment so each rank's owned slice maps
771	    back to the right param sub-ranges), which is easy to get subtly wrong and
772	    cannot be validated without a real multi-GPU job. The risk outweighs the
773	    value for the race's small models, so it is deferred to the DeepSpeed path
774	    (``build_ds_config`` already sets ``contiguous_gradients=True`` and the
775	    bucket sizes). The DDP (ZeRO-0/1/2) path *is* bucketed — see
776	    :meth:`DistributedContext.all_reduce_dp_grads`.
777	    """
778	
779	    def __init__(self, ctx: DistributedContext) -> None:
780	        self.ctx = ctx
781	        self.use_deepspeed = deepspeed_available()
782	        # name -> _ParamShard for this rank (native shim only).
783	        self._shards: Dict[str, _ParamShard] = {}
784	
785	    @property
786	    def dp_world(self) -> int:
787	        return self.ctx.dp_world_size
788	
789	    @property
790	    def dp_rank(self) -> int:
791	        return self.ctx.dp_rank

795	    def build_ds_config(
796	        self,
797	        train_micro_batch_size_per_gpu: int = 1,
798	        gradient_accumulation_steps: int = 1,
799	        bf16: bool = True,
800	        offload_optimizer: bool = False,
801	    ) -> Dict:
802	        """Emit a DeepSpeed ZeRO-3 config dict matching this context's stage.
803	
804	        Pure data — does not import or call DeepSpeed, so it is import-safe even
805	        when DeepSpeed is absent (useful for serializing the launch config).
806	        """
807	        # Cross-node all-gather/reduce-scatter bucket sizes. These are the knobs
808	        # §8.6/§2.13 cares about: on AMD multinode the cross-node all-gather is
809	        # the bottleneck, so larger buckets amortize launch latency. Honor the
810	        # context's configured ``reduce_bucket_size`` (no longer hardcoded 5M),
811	        # so the native DDP path and the DeepSpeed path use ONE source of truth.
812	        # The prefetch/persistence knobs scale off it so they stay proportional.
813	        bucket = self.ctx.config.reduce_bucket_size
814	        zero: Dict = {
815	            "stage": self.ctx.config.zero_stage,
816	            "reduce_bucket_size": bucket,
817	            "stage3_prefetch_bucket_size": bucket,
818	            "stage3_param_persistence_threshold": 1_000_000,
819	            "stage3_max_live_parameters": 1_000_000_000,
820	            "stage3_gather_16bit_weights_on_model_save": True,
821	            "contiguous_gradients": True,
822	            "overlap_comm": True,
823	        }
824	        if offload_optimizer:
825	            zero["offload_optimizer"] = {"device": "cpu", "pin_memory": True}
826	        cfg: Dict = {
827	            "train_micro_batch_size_per_gpu": train_micro_batch_size_per_gpu,
828	            "gradient_accumulation_steps": gradient_accumulation_steps,
829	            "zero_optimization": zero,
830	        }
831	        if bf16:
832	            cfg["bf16"] = {"enabled": True}

837	    def partition_optimizer_state(
838	        self, named_params: Iterable[Tuple[str, "torch.Tensor"]]
839	    ) -> Dict[str, _ParamShard]:
840	        """Assign this DP rank its contiguous ``1/N`` slice of every parameter.
841	
842	        Records the shard map used by :meth:`reduce_scatter_grads` /
843	        :meth:`all_gather_params`. The optimizer then only allocates state
844	        (m/v/…) for ``[start:end)`` of each param — the ZeRO-3 memory win.
845	        Single-process ⇒ every shard is the whole param (a clean degenerate).
846	        """
847	        self._shards.clear()
848	        world = self.dp_world
849	        rank = self.dp_rank
850	        for name, p in named_params:
851	            numel = p.numel()
852	            start, end = _even_partition(numel, world, rank)
853	            self._shards[name] = _ParamShard(name, numel, start, end)
854	        return dict(self._shards)
855	
856	    def owned_slice(self, name: str, tensor: "torch.Tensor") -> "torch.Tensor":
857	        """Return this rank's owned flat slice of ``tensor`` (or all of it)."""
858	        shard = self._shards.get(name)
859	        flat = tensor.reshape(-1)
860	        if shard is None:
861	            return flat
862	        return flat[shard.start:shard.end]
863	
864	    def reduce_scatter_grads(
865	        self, named_grads: Iterable[Tuple[str, "torch.Tensor"]]
866	    ) -> Dict[str, "torch.Tensor"]:
867	        """ZeRO-3 gradient reduce-scatter across the DP group.
868	
869	        Each rank receives the *summed-then-averaged* gradient for **only its
870	        owned slice** of each parameter — the input the sharded local optimizer
871	        step consumes. Falls back to a plain copy of the local grad slice when
872	        DP size is 1 / no job is launched (single-process correctness).
873	
874	        Implementation: a true fused ``reduce_scatter_tensor`` per parameter —
875	        each rank sends the whole (per-rank-padded) flat grad and receives only
876	        the reduced sum for its owned slice, which is half the traffic of the
877	        former ``all_reduce``-then-slice. The padded reduce-scatter convention
878	        matches :meth:`all_gather_params` / :meth:`_even_partition` (each rank
879	        owns ``ceil(numel/world)`` elements). Falls back to the local slice when
880	        DP size is 1 / no job is launched (single-process correctness).
881	        """
882	        out: Dict[str, "torch.Tensor"] = {}
883	        live = self.dp_world > 1 and is_dist_available_and_initialized()
884	        ws = self.dp_world
885	        if not live:
886	            for name, g in named_grads:
887	                out[name] = self.owned_slice(name, g).clone()
888	            return out
889	
890	        dist = _dist()
891	        group = self.ctx.dp_group
892	        rstensor = getattr(dist, "reduce_scatter_tensor", None)
893	        for name, g in named_grads:
894	            flat = g.reshape(-1).contiguous()
895	            numel = flat.numel()
896	            per = (numel + ws - 1) // ws
897	            if rstensor is not None:
898	                # Pad the input to world*per so the scatter is uniform.
899	                padded = flat
900	                if per * ws != numel:
901	                    padded = flat.new_zeros(per * ws)
902	                    padded[:numel] = flat
903	                owned = flat.new_empty(per)
904	                rstensor(owned, padded, group=group)
905	                owned.div_(ws)
906	                # Trim padding off this rank's owned slice.
907	                shard = self._shards.get(name)
908	                keep = (shard.shard_numel if shard is not None
909	                        else max(0, min(per, numel - self.dp_rank * per)))
910	                out[name] = owned[:keep].clone()
911	            else:
912	                # Older torch without reduce_scatter_tensor: equivalent result
913	                # via all_reduce + owned slice.
914	                dist.all_reduce(flat, group=group)
915	                flat.div_(ws)
916	                out[name] = self.owned_slice(name, flat).clone()
917	        return out
918	
919	    def all_gather_params(
920	        self, named_params: Iterable[Tuple[str, "torch.Tensor"]]
921	    ) -> None:
922	        """ZeRO-3 all-gather-on-step: reconstitute full params from DP slices.
923	
924	        After each DP rank updates its owned slice, every rank needs the full
925	        parameter again for the next forward/backward. We use a fused
926	        ``all_gather_into_tensor`` (single contiguous output buffer) instead of
927	        the list-based ``all_gather``, then stitch the per-rank slices back into
928	        the param in place. No-op single-process. This is the §2.13
929	        cross-node-sensitive collective (the AMD multinode gap the harness
930	        records).
931	        """
932	        if self.dp_world <= 1 or not is_dist_available_and_initialized():
933	            return
934	        dist = _dist()
935	        world = self.dp_world
936	        group = self.ctx.dp_group
937	        agtensor = getattr(dist, "all_gather_into_tensor", None)
938	        for name, p in named_params:
939	            shard = self._shards.get(name)
940	            if shard is None:
941	                continue
942	            flat = p.reshape(-1)
943	            owned = flat[shard.start:shard.end].contiguous()
944	            # Pad to the common per-rank shard length so the gather is uniform.
945	            per = (shard.numel + world - 1) // world
946	            buf = owned.new_zeros(per)
947	            buf[: owned.numel()] = owned
948	            if agtensor is not None:
949	                gathered = buf.new_empty(per * world)
950	                agtensor(gathered, buf, group=group)
951	                # Stitch the contiguous [r*per:(r+1)*per] slices back in place.
952	                for r in range(world):
953	                    start = min(r * per, shard.numel)
954	                    end = min(start + per, shard.numel)
955	                    n = end - start
956	                    if n > 0:
957	                        flat[start:end].copy_(gathered[r * per:r * per + n])
958	            else:
959	                gathered = [torch.empty_like(buf) for _ in range(world)]
960	                dist.all_gather(gathered, buf, group=group)
961	                for r in range(world):
962	                    start = min(r * per, shard.numel)
963	                    end = min(start + per, shard.numel)
964	                    n = end - start
965	                    if n > 0:
966	                        flat[start:end].copy_(gathered[r][:n])
967	
968	
969	__all__ = [
970	    "ParallelConfig",
971	    "DistributedContext",
972	    "get_distributed_context",
973	    "is_dist_available_and_initialized",
974	    "deepspeed_available",
975	    "ZeRO3Sharder",
976	]

1	"""grokking_optimizers.megakernel_engine — §8.4 fused-kernel ↔ framework adapter.
2	
3	THE TRICKY PART (§8.4). DeepSpeed and Megatron-LM are both built around a
4	**separate** forward / backward / `optimizer.step()` interface:
5	
6	    out  = engine(batch)        # forward
7	    engine.backward(loss)       # backward — populates .grad on every param
8	    engine.step()               # optimizer.step() + grad clear
9	
10	But the Stage-6 megakernel (``grokking_optimizers.megakernel``) is a **fused L3
11	single launch**: one persistent kernel does forward **and** backward **and** the
12	optimizer update inside one kernel invocation (``FusionTier.L3_FWD_BWD_OPT``).
13	There is no separate backward to hook, and no separate `.step()` — the fused
14	launch already did all three. The framework's contract and the fused kernel's
15	contract are therefore in direct conflict.
16	
17	This module is the **adapter** that reconciles them. It does two things:
18	
19	1. :class:`MegakernelOptimizer` — a ``torch.optim.Optimizer`` subclass that
20	   presents the fused step as a standard ``.step()`` so DeepSpeed/Megatron can
21	   drive it as a ``client_optimizer``. Its ``.step()`` is where the actual fused
22	   launch is invoked (for L3) or where the inner optimizer's real ``.step()``
23	   runs (for L1/L2). It degrades to a plain pass-through optimizer when no
24	   framework is present.
25	
26	2. :class:`FusedBackwardHook` — intercepts / no-ops the framework's separate
27	   ``.backward()`` **when the fused path owns fwd+bwd+opt** (L3). When the fused
28	   kernel already produced gradients-and-update in the forward launch, letting
29	   the framework run its own autograd backward would (a) waste a full backward
30	   pass and (b) double-apply the update. The hook short-circuits the framework
31	   backward and instead just marks gradients as "owned by the fused kernel" so
32	   ``.step()`` knows not to re-run them.
33	
34	The decision of *which* mode a given (model, optimizer, arch) cell is in comes
35	from the Stage-6 solver: :func:`grokking_optimizers.megakernel.solve` returns a
36	:class:`~grokking_optimizers.megakernel.FusionPlan` whose ``tier`` tells us how
37	much the fused kernel owns. The control flow below is keyed entirely off that
38	tier.
39	
40	────────────────────────────── CONTROL FLOW ──────────────────────────────────
41	
42	  query solve(model, optimizer, arch) → plan.tier
43	
44	  ┌─ L3_FWD_BWD_OPT  (fused kernel owns fwd + bwd + opt) ─────────────────────┐
45	  │  forward(batch):                                                          │
46	  │     • the fused L3 launch runs fwd+bwd+opt in ONE kernel.                 │
47	  │     • returns loss; gradients + the parameter update are ALREADY applied. │
48	  │     • adapter sets `_fused_owned = True`.                                 │
49	  │  engine.backward(loss):                                                   │
50	  │     • FusedBackwardHook.intercepts() → True → **NO-OP**. The framework's  │
51	  │       autograd backward is suppressed (it would redo work + double-apply).│
52	  │  engine.step()  →  MegakernelOptimizer.step():                           │
53	  │     • sees `_fused_owned` → the update already happened in forward → it   │
54	  │       only does framework bookkeeping (zero_grad bookkeeping, lr-sched    │
55	  │       coupling) and returns. It does NOT re-run the optimizer math.       │
56	  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
57	
58	  ┌─ L2_BWD_OPT  (fused kernel owns bwd + opt; framework owns fwd) ───────────┐
59	  │  forward(batch):  framework's normal forward (autograd graph built).      │
60	  │  engine.backward(loss):                                                   │
61	  │     • FusedBackwardHook.intercepts() → True for the FUSED region: the     │
62	  │       fused bwd+opt launch runs, producing grads + applying the update.   │
63	  │     • framework autograd backward is suppressed for the fused params.     │
64	  │  engine.step():  update already applied by the fused bwd+opt → no-op math.│
65	  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
66	
67	  ┌─ L1_OPT_ONLY  (fused kernel owns ONLY the optimizer step) ────────────────┐
68	  │  forward(batch):  framework forward.                                      │
69	  │  engine.backward(loss):                                                   │
70	  │     • FusedBackwardHook.intercepts() → False → framework runs its OWN     │
71	  │       autograd backward normally (grads populated the usual way).         │
72	  │  engine.step()  →  MegakernelOptimizer.step():                           │
73	  │     • runs the fused optimizer-only kernel via the wrapped optimizer's    │
74	  │       real `.step()` (which itself dispatches to the L1 fused tail).      │
75	  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
76	
77	  ┌─ L0_UNFUSED  (no fusion — solver would have errored for a megakernel) ────┐
78	  │  Pure pass-through: framework fwd, framework bwd, wrapped optimizer step. │
79	  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
80	
81	IMPORT SAFETY. This module imports only ``torch`` and the pure-Python Stage-6
82	solver at module load. The DeepSpeed / Megatron framework objects are *never*
83	imported here; the adapter is shaped to fit their duck-typed `client_optimizer`
84	/ backward-hook protocols, so it works when they are present and degrades to a
85	plain torch optimizer when they are absent. No GPU, no launched job, and no
86	DeepSpeed are required to import or unit-test the dispatch logic.
87	"""
88	
89	from __future__ import annotations
90	
91	from typing import Any, Callable, Iterable, Optional
92	
93	import torch
94	from torch.optim import Optimizer
95	
96	from grokking_optimizers.megakernel import FusionPlan, FusionTier, solve
97	
98	
99	# ─────────────────────── unified cross-arch fused dispatch ───────────────────
100	
101	def dispatch_fused_megakernel(model: str, optimizer: str, *, params=None,
102	                              grads=None, opt_state=None, inputs=None,
103	                              lr: float = 1e-3, state=None):
104	    """Route a fused L3/L1 megakernel step to the backend for the detected arch.
105	
106	    The single cross-arch entry that unifies the three real composition paths
107	    (Phase 3):
108	      * tpu_v6e → csrc.backends.pallas._pallas_fused.fused_step (jax.jit fused
109	        program; the 33 tpu cells bind to it).
110	      * sm_90 / gfx942 → the C++ `fused_step` pybind (dispatch.cpp routes to the
111	        real composed `mega_<model>_<opt>` launcher; gfx942 host launch is 🟡).
112	
113	    Returns the backend's result (TPU: (new_params, new_state)). Raises a clear
114	    error if the cell/binding is unavailable on this build (no silent no-op).
115	    """
116	    from grokking_optimizers.dispatch import detect_arch, normalize_arch
117	    arch = detect_arch()
118	    # detect_arch() now reports the REAL arch (e.g. sm_80 / sm_90a / gfx942).
119	    # The megakernel solver keys on the impl-family label ("sm_90"/"gfx942"/
120	    # "tpu_v6e"), so normalise the real arch to its family for the solve() call.
121	    impl = normalize_arch(arch)
122	    solver_arch = (impl if isinstance(impl, str)
123	                   else ("sm_90" if impl == 90 else "gfx942"))
124	    tier = ("L3" if solve(model, optimizer, solver_arch).tier
125	            == FusionTier.L3_FWD_BWD_OPT else "L1")
126	    if arch == "tpu_v6e":
127	        from csrc.backends.pallas._pallas_fused import fused_step as tpu_fused
128	        return tpu_fused(model, optimizer, params=params, grads=grads,
129	                         opt_state=opt_state, inputs=inputs, lr=lr, tier=tier)
130	    # NVIDIA / AMD: the C++ megakernel dispatch (real composition per dispatch.cpp).
131	    from grokking_optimizers.dispatch import get_ops
132	    ops = get_ops()
133	    if not hasattr(ops, "fused_step"):
134	        raise RuntimeError(
135	            "C++ fused_step binding unavailable; build the extension "
136	            "(WITH_CUDA/WITH_HIP) to use the GPU fused megakernel path.")
137	    if params is None or state is None:
138	        raise ValueError("GPU fused_step needs params, grads, and a state tensor "
139	                         "([m|v|extra] per param-tensor).")
140	    # PURE L3-TC (task #10): the L1 optimizer-only tail and the scalar fp32 engine
141	    # were removed — there is no lesser path left to invoke. If the solver does not
142	    # award this cell the full L3 fwd+bwd+opt tier, hard-fail loudly rather than
143	    # silently calling a path that no longer exists (owner directive: L3-TC or
144	    # hard-fail, never a silent downgrade). When L3, drive the only surviving entry:
145	    # opt_only=False + gemm_impl="wgmma". NOTE: this adapter binds only lr (the scalar
146	    # set keeps the inert ABI defaults); a caller needing real bias correction /
147	    # per-optimizer scalars should use grokking_optimizers.dispatch.fused_train_step,
148	    # the full-scalar driver the race uses.
149	    if tier != "L3":
150	        raise RuntimeError(
151	            f"megakernel_engine.fused_step: solver did not award ({model}, "
152	            f"{optimizer}, {solver_arch}) the L3 fwd+bwd+opt tier (got {tier!r}); "
153	            "the L1/scalar fallback was removed (pure L3-TC). Investigate the "
154	            "solver/cost model rather than downgrading to a path that no longer exists.")
155	    ops.fused_step(model, optimizer, params,
156	                   inputs if inputs is not None else params,
157	                   grads if grads is not None else params, state, float(lr),
158	                   opt_only=False, gemm_impl="wgmma")
159	    return params
160	
161	
162	# ─────────────────────────── fused-ownership query ───────────────────────────
163	
164	
165	def resolve_fusion_plan(
166	    model_name: str, optimizer_name: str, arch: str
167	) -> Optional[FusionPlan]:
168	    """Query the Stage-6 solver for the (model, optimizer, arch) fusion plan.
169	
170	    Returns ``None`` (not an error) when the cell is infeasible or the names are
171	    unknown — the adapter then falls back to the fully-unfused pass-through path,
172	    which is always correct. This keeps the adapter import-safe and robust to a
173	    model/optimizer the solver doesn't model.
174	    """
175	    try:
176	        return solve(model_name, optimizer_name, arch)
177	    except (KeyError, RuntimeError):
178	        return None
179	
180	
181	def _tier_of(plan: Optional[FusionPlan]) -> FusionTier:
182	    return plan.tier if plan is not None else FusionTier.L0_UNFUSED
183	
184	
185	def fused_owns_backward(plan: Optional[FusionPlan]) -> bool:
186	    """True iff the fused kernel owns the backward pass (tiers L2/L3).
187	
188	    When True, the framework's separate ``.backward()`` must be suppressed by
189	    :class:`FusedBackwardHook` to avoid redundant work + a double parameter
190	    update.
191	    """
192	    return _tier_of(plan) >= FusionTier.L2_BWD_OPT
193	
194	
195	def fused_owns_step(plan: Optional[FusionPlan]) -> bool:
196	    """True iff the fused kernel already applied the optimizer update inside the
197	    fused launch (tiers L2/L3). When True, ``.step()`` must NOT re-run the math.
198	    """
199	    return _tier_of(plan) >= FusionTier.L2_BWD_OPT
200	
201	
202	# ─────────────────────────── FusedBackwardHook ───────────────────────────────
203	
204	
205	class FusedBackwardHook:
206	    """Intercepts / no-ops the framework's separate backward when fused (§8.4).
207	
208	    Usage shapes (both duck-typed, framework-agnostic):
209	
210	    * **Explicit guard** — wrap the framework backward call::
211	
212	          if not hook.intercept_backward(loss):
213	              engine.backward(loss)   # framework path (L0/L1 only)
214	
215	      ``intercept_backward`` returns True when the fused kernel already owns the
216	      backward (L2/L3), in which case the framework backward is skipped and the
217	      fused launch is invoked instead.
218	
219	    * **Tensor hook** — :meth:`as_tensor_hook` returns a callable suitable for
220	      ``loss.register_hook(...)`` that zeroes the incoming grad when the fused
221	      path owns it, so an accidental ``loss.backward()`` is neutralized rather
222	      than double-applying.
223	    """
224	
225	    def __init__(
226	        self,
227	        plan: Optional[FusionPlan],
228	        fused_launch: Optional[Callable[..., Any]] = None,
229	    ) -> None:
230	        self.plan = plan
231	        # The callable that actually performs the fused bwd(+opt) launch. In the
232	        # real build this routes into the dispatch.cpp fused TU; here it is
233	        # injected so the control flow is testable without a kernel.
234	        self._fused_launch = fused_launch
235	        # Set True after a fused launch has applied the update this iteration,
236	        # so MegakernelOptimizer.step() knows the math already ran.
237	        self.fused_update_applied = False
238	
239	    @property
240	    def owns_backward(self) -> bool:
241	        return fused_owns_backward(self.plan)
242	
243	    def intercept_backward(self, loss: "torch.Tensor", **kwargs: Any) -> bool:
244	        """Decide whether to suppress the framework backward.
245	
246	        Returns
247	        -------
248	        bool
249	            True  → the fused kernel owns backward (L2/L3); the framework's
250	                    ``.backward()`` was suppressed and the fused launch (if
251	                    provided) was invoked here instead.
252	            False → L0/L1; the caller must run the framework backward itself.
253	        """
254	        if not self.owns_backward:
255	            return False
256	        # Fused path owns backward: run the fused launch (bwd[+opt]) if wired,
257	        # and mark the update as applied so .step() is a no-op on the math.
258	        if self._fused_launch is not None:
259	            self._fused_launch(loss, **kwargs)
260	        self.fused_update_applied = fused_owns_step(self.plan)
261	        return True
262	
263	    def as_tensor_hook(self) -> Callable[["torch.Tensor"], "torch.Tensor"]:
264	        """Return a ``Tensor.register_hook`` callable that neutralizes grads.
265	
266	        If the fused path owns backward and an autograd backward is nonetheless
267	        triggered, this zeroes the gradient flowing back so nothing is
268	        double-counted. A pass-through (identity) when the framework legitimately
269	        owns backward (L0/L1).
270	        """
271	
272	        owns = self.owns_backward
273	
274	        def _hook(grad: "torch.Tensor") -> "torch.Tensor":
275	            if owns:
276	                return torch.zeros_like(grad)
277	            return grad
278	
279	        return _hook
280	
281	    def reset(self) -> None:
282	        """Clear per-iteration state (call at the top of each training step)."""
283	        self.fused_update_applied = False
284	
285	
286	# ─────────────────────────── MegakernelOptimizer ─────────────────────────────
287	
288	
289	class MegakernelOptimizer(Optimizer):
290	    """Present the fused L3 megakernel step as a standard ``torch.optim`` step.
291	
292	    Wraps an *inner* optimizer (one of the 11 race optimizers — an
293	    ``Optimizer`` whose real ``.step()`` dispatches into the fused kernel for the
294	    L1 optimizer-only tail). Depending on the fusion tier reported by the
295	    Stage-6 solver, ``.step()`` either:
296	
297	    * **L3 / L2** — the fused launch (driven through :class:`FusedBackwardHook`
298	      during the forward/backward phase) already applied the parameter update;
299	      ``.step()`` performs only framework bookkeeping and returns. It does NOT
300	      re-run the optimizer math (that would double-apply).
301	    * **L1 / L0** — calls the inner optimizer's real ``.step()`` (which itself
302	      fuses the optimizer-only tail at L1, or runs unfused at L0).
303	
304	    The class satisfies DeepSpeed's ``client_optimizer`` shape: it subclasses
305	    ``torch.optim.Optimizer``, exposes ``param_groups`` / ``state`` (delegated to
306	    the inner optimizer), and a no-arg-compatible ``.step()``. With no framework
307	    present it behaves as a transparent wrapper around the inner optimizer.
308	    """
309	
310	    def __init__(
311	        self,
312	        inner_optimizer: Optimizer,
313	        model_name: str,
314	        arch: str,
315	        optimizer_name: Optional[str] = None,
316	        hook: Optional[FusedBackwardHook] = None,
317	    ) -> None:
318	        if not isinstance(inner_optimizer, Optimizer):
319	            raise TypeError(
320	                "inner_optimizer must be a torch.optim.Optimizer, got "
321	                f"{type(inner_optimizer).__name__}"
322	            )
323	        self.inner = inner_optimizer
324	        self.model_name = model_name
325	        self.arch = arch
326	        self.optimizer_name = optimizer_name or _infer_optimizer_name(inner_optimizer)
327	        self.plan = resolve_fusion_plan(self.model_name, self.optimizer_name, self.arch)
328	        self.hook = hook or FusedBackwardHook(self.plan)
329	        # We deliberately do NOT call super().__init__ with fresh defaults — we
330	        # delegate param_groups/state to the inner optimizer so DeepSpeed sees
331	        # the real parameters, learning rates, and state. The Optimizer
332	        # protocol only requires param_groups + state + step + zero_grad, all of
333	        # which we forward.
334	        self.defaults = getattr(inner_optimizer, "defaults", {})
335	
336	    # ── Optimizer protocol delegation (DeepSpeed client_optimizer shape) ─────
337	
338	    @property
339	    def param_groups(self):  # type: ignore[override]
340	        return self.inner.param_groups
341	
342	    @param_groups.setter
343	    def param_groups(self, value):  # type: ignore[override]
344	        self.inner.param_groups = value
345	
346	    @property
347	    def state(self):  # type: ignore[override]
348	        return self.inner.state
349	
350	    @state.setter
351	    def state(self, value):  # type: ignore[override]
352	        self.inner.state = value
353	
354	    def state_dict(self):
355	        return self.inner.state_dict()
356	
357	    def load_state_dict(self, state_dict):
358	        return self.inner.load_state_dict(state_dict)
359	
360	    def zero_grad(self, set_to_none: bool = True):  # type: ignore[override]
361	        return self.inner.zero_grad(set_to_none=set_to_none)
362	
363	    def add_param_group(self, param_group):
364	        return self.inner.add_param_group(param_group)
365	
366	    # ── the fused-aware step (the §8.4 reconciliation point) ─────────────────
367	
368	    @torch.no_grad()
369	    def step(self, closure: Optional[Callable[[], float]] = None):  # type: ignore[override]
370	        """Fused-aware optimizer step.
371	
372	        Control flow (mirrors the module docstring):
373	
374	        * If the fused kernel already applied the update this iteration
375	          (``hook.fused_update_applied`` — set by :class:`FusedBackwardHook` for
376	          L2/L3), the math is **already done**: we only run the closure (for
377	          loss reporting) and reset the hook, then return. Re-running
378	          ``inner.step()`` here would double-apply the update.
379	        * Otherwise (L0/L1, or no fused launch happened), delegate to the inner
380	          optimizer's real ``.step()`` — which fuses the optimizer-only tail at
381	          L1 or runs unfused at L0.
382	        """
383	        loss = None
384	        if closure is not None:
385	            with torch.enable_grad():
386	                loss = closure()
387	
388	        if fused_owns_step(self.plan) and self.hook.fused_update_applied:
389	            # L2/L3 fused path already updated the params in the fused launch.
390	            # Bookkeeping only — do NOT re-run the optimizer math.
391	            self.hook.reset()
392	            return loss
393	
394	        # L0/L1 (or fused launch did not run this step): real optimizer step.
395	        result = self.inner.step()
396	        self.hook.reset()
397	        return loss if loss is not None else result

405	        which case the caller must NOT also run the framework autograd backward.
406	        Returns False for L0/L1, signalling the caller to run its own backward.
407	        """

466	    optimizer: MegakernelOptimizer,

468	    framework_backward: Optional[Callable[["torch.Tensor"], None]] = None,
469	) -> None:
470	    """Reference glue for one fused-aware training step (§8.4 control flow).
471	
472	    Encapsulates the backward/step reconciliation so a framework loop (or the
473	    test harness) can call a single function:
474	
475	        1. Ask the hook whether the fused kernel owns backward.
476	        2. If not (L0/L1), run ``framework_backward(loss)`` (the engine's
477	           autograd backward).
478	        3. Call ``optimizer.step()`` — which is a no-op on the math for L2/L3
479	           (already applied) and the real step for L0/L1.
480	
481	    ``framework_backward`` defaults to ``loss.backward`` when not supplied.
482	    """
483	    if not optimizer.backward(loss):
484	        bwd = framework_backward or (lambda x: x.backward())
485	        bwd(loss)

491	) -> None:

493	
494	    Several race optimizers (notably SuperGrok2 via ``_allreduce_meta_grads`` /
495	    ``_allreduce_expert_counts``) already carry DP-aware allreduce hooks. The
496	    distributed layer calls this before the fused step so those hooks fire under
497	    the launched job; it is a guarded no-op when the hooks/job are absent.
498	    """
499	    inner = getattr(optimizer, "inner", optimizer)
500	    for hook_name in ("_allreduce_meta_grads", "_allreduce_expert_counts"):
501	        fn = getattr(inner, hook_name, None)
502	        if callable(fn):
503	            try:
504	                fn()
505	            except Exception:
506	                # Hooks self-guard on dist.is_initialized(); never fatal here.
507	                pass

158	def _build_sharded_binding():
159	    """Load the DELIVERABLE-1 sharded-opt JIT binding (shared build cache)."""
